text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Zimbabwe's government pressing its planning commission to pay Z$100 million to Cyprus-based Hazy Investments, the company it awarded a tender to design and built a new terminal at Harare airport, official sources said. Parliament has refused to ratify loans to finance the project.

- A salaries advisory board has recommended that Zimbabwe's current wage negotiations take into account "the plight of workers whose real income has collapsed" over the years. Unions are demanding wage increases of around 25 percent.
- Zimbabwe's automotive and oil industries have been gripped by allegations that contaminated fuel is being sold to motorists.
- Zimbabwe is still expected to meet earlier forecasts that its sugar production will reach a record 600,000 tonnes this year, following a good rainy season, an industry official said.
- Zimbabwe's main dairy company, Dairiboard, has increased the wholesale price of fresh milk and dairy products by 15 percent, citing an escalation in the cost of packaging material.
